name: Saint Martha
history: The sister of Mary and Lazarus of Bethany, whose house was a home to Christ. Saint Luke tells of her busy with serving while Mary sat at His feet; Saint John records her great confession of faith at the tomb of Lazarus. Since 2021 the Church keeps the three siblings together on this day. She is the patron of cooks and of all who serve.
life: Martha appears in the Gospels as practical, warm and direct. When Christ came to the house at Bethany, she was distracted with much serving and asked Him to tell her sister to help, and He answered gently, ‘Martha, Martha, you are anxious and troubled about many things; one thing is needful.’ When Lazarus died, it was Martha who went out to meet Jesus and said, ‘Lord, if You had been here, my brother would not have died.’ He told her, ‘I am the resurrection and the life,’ and she answered, ‘Yes, Lord, I believe that You are the Christ, the Son of God.’ At a supper six days before the Passover, after Lazarus had been raised, Martha served again. A medieval tradition says she later went to Provence and tamed a dragon at Tarascon, where she is honoured to this day.
prayerTo: Saint Martha, you welcomed Christ into your home and served Him with your hands, and you believed in Him when your brother lay in the tomb. Pray for all who cook, clean and care for others, and for me, that I may not be anxious about many things, but choose the one thing needful. Amen.
penance: Cook a meal or do a household task for someone today as an act of love, and then take ten quiet minutes, like Mary, at the Lord’s feet.
meditation: One thing is needful. What are the many things that are crowding it out today?
prayer: Hear us, O God, our Saviour, that as we are gladdened by the festival of blessed Martha thy virgin, so we may learn from it piety and devotion. Through our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
prayerSource: Collect of the day, Roman Missal of 1962
